491	    # failed on mere overlap would have failed all four correct promotions, and would fail
492	    # the next batch's promotion of REF-00327/576/577/579 as well.
493	    #
494	    # The real defect is one source wearing two identities, and it runs in both directions:
495	    #   R9a  this batch admitted DOI D as ref_id Y, but the stash already holds D as X != Y
496	    #   R9b  this batch admitted ref_id R, but the stash holds R against a DIFFERENT DOI
497	    # R9b is not hypothetical: there is no next_ref_id allocator (CLAUDE.md 4), so a batch
498	    # that mints below the stash high-water mark collides with a held identifier in silence.
499	    escope = "" if allmode else " AND e.created_by_session = ?"
500	
501	    # SUBJECT COUNT FIRST. Adversarial pass 2026-08-23 found R9a/R9b printing a bare
502	    # "PASS" for a session that admitted nothing -- CLAUDE.md 2(a), a gate that passes
503	    # having examined nothing, reproduced inside the fix written for a gate that examined
504	    # the WRONG set. Both rules now carry their subject count, and say so when it is zero.
505	    # WIDENED TO URL 2026-09-17. The subject was DOI-bearing admissions ALONE, so a batch
506	    # whose sources legitimately have no DOI -- every Co-1, DPO, grey and regulatory source
507	    # there is -- fell into the zero-branch below and was told it had admitted nothing and
508	    # was "missing its locators". Both halves were false for batch 09, which admitted two
509	    # sources each carrying a URL. The stash holds 402 URLs against 465 DOIs (derive it:
510	    # SELECT COUNT(*) FROM source_locators WHERE COALESCE(url,'') <> ''), so the check
511	    # could be performed and simply was not. This is R9b's own 2026-08-23 widening applied
512	    # to R9a: CLAUDE.md §4's warning is not DOI-conditional, and neither is identity.
513	    n_doi = _rows(cx, f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM evidence_sources e WHERE COALESCE(e.doi,'') <> ''"
514	                      f"{escope}", sargs)[0][0]
515	    n_url = _rows(cx, f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM evidence_sources e WHERE COALESCE(e.doi,'') = '' "
516	                      f"AND COALESCE(e.url,'') <> ''{escope}", sargs)[0][0]
517	    n_adm = _rows(cx, f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM evidence_sources e WHERE 1=1{escope}", sargs)[0][0]
518	    # DID THIS SESSION LOOK? The difference between "admitted nothing AFTER SEARCHING" and
519	    # "did nothing" is the whole of the zero-yield question, and the search log is what
520	    # settles it -- derived, not a sentinel row anyone has to remember to write. R14 is
521	    # explicit that a zero-yield search is "a COMPLETED unit of work", so a batch that
522	    # searched honestly and admitted nothing is COMPLIANT doctrine; before 2026-09-17 it was
523	    # non-compliant machinery, and once research_dod_session became blocking that combination
524	    # would have stopped CI for a batch that did exactly what the contract asks.
525	    n_search = _rows(cx, f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM search_executions WHERE 1=1"
526	                         f"{' AND created_by_session = ?' if not allmode else ''}", sargs)[0][0]
527	
528	    # RETIRED STASH ROWS ARE NOT A HELD IDENTITY, AND EXCLUDING THEM IS THE WHOLE POINT
529	    # OF THE TOMBSTONE. Migration 076 retains the thirteen refs the 2026-09-13 clear deleted
530	    # as `source_locators` rows with status RETIRED, precisely so their ref_ids are never
531	    # reissued. R9a's remedy -- "cross-file the held id instead of minting a second" -- is
532	    # therefore IMPOSSIBLE against one: cross-filing to REF-00973 would reuse a retired
533	    # identifier, which is the one thing 076 exists to prevent. Without this clause the two
534	    # requirements contradict each other for exactly the set the clear produced, and the
535	    # re-run the same ruling ordered cannot admit a single cleared source by any route.
536	    # Found by batch 08, whose cell (TERM-001 ramp gradient) has REF-00979 and REF-00980 --
537	    # the two most on-point ramp-slope papers in the prior corpus -- among the tombstones.
538	    # R9b IS DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED. It joins on ref_id, not DOI, and a tombstone blocking
539	    # a batch from minting a ref_id the stash still holds is that rule working as intended.
540	    split = _rows(cx, f"SELECT e.ref_id, sl.ref_id, e.doi FROM evidence_sources e "
541	                      f"JOIN source_locators sl ON LOWER(TRIM(sl.doi)) = LOWER(TRIM(e.doi)) "
542	                      f"WHERE COALESCE(e.doi,'') <> '' AND COALESCE(sl.doi,'') <> '' "
543	                      f"AND COALESCE(sl.status,'') <> 'RETIRED' "
544	                      f"AND sl.ref_id <> e.ref_id{escope}", sargs)
545	
546	    # A URL IS A HELD IDENTITY ONLY WHEN IT IDENTIFIES EXACTLY ONE SOURCE, and that
547	    # restriction is the whole design rather than a refinement of it. Measured 2026-09-17
548	    # before this was written: the BSI catalogue page for BS 8300 is held against SEVEN
549	    # different ref_ids, the ISO and DIN catalogue pages and the ADA standards page against
550	    # five each. Those are LANDING PAGES -- one web address serving a whole standards family
551	    # -- and sharing one is correct, not a defect. A naive url join would have fired on every
552	    # one of them and told the operator to "cross-file the held id", which for two genuinely
553	    # different standards is wrong advice that destroys an identity rather than repairing one.
554	    # So the set is derived, never assumed: a url the stash resolves to a single ref_id is an
555	    # identity; a url it resolves to several is a catalogue, and proves nothing either way.
556	    # Derive the split rather than trusting this comment:
557	    #   SELECT LOWER(TRIM(url)), COUNT(DISTINCT ref_id) n FROM source_locators
558	    #   WHERE COALESCE(url,'') <> '' GROUP BY 1 HAVING n > 1;
559	    urlnorm = "RTRIM(LOWER(TRIM({}.url)), '/')"
560	    singleton = (f"SELECT {urlnorm.format('s2')} FROM source_locators s2 "
561	                 f"WHERE COALESCE(s2.url,'') <> '' AND COALESCE(s2.status,'') <> 'RETIRED' "
562	                 f"GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT s2.ref_id) = 1")
563	    usplit = _rows(cx, f"SELECT e.ref_id, sl.ref_id, e.url FROM evidence_sources e "
564	                       f"JOIN source_locators sl ON {urlnorm.format('sl')} = {urlnorm.format('e')} "
565	                       f"WHERE COALESCE(e.url,'') <> '' AND COALESCE(sl.url,'') <> '' "
566	                       f"AND COALESCE(sl.status,'') <> 'RETIRED' "
567	                       f"AND sl.ref_id <> e.ref_id "
568	                       f"AND {urlnorm.format('sl')} IN ({singleton}){escope}", sargs)
569	
570	    if split or usplit:
571	        both = [(a, b, d, "DOI") for a, b, d in split] + [(a, b, u, "URL") for a, b, u in usplit]
572	        fail("R9a", f"{len(both)} source(s) admitted under a ref_id that DIFFERS from the one "
573	                    f"the identifier stash already holds for the same identifier — one source, "
574	                    f"two identities. Cross-file the held id instead of minting a second: "
575	                    + "; ".join(f"{a} vs stash {b} ({k} {d})" for a, b, d, k in both[:5]),
576	             len(both))
577	    elif n_doi == 0 and n_url == 0:
578	        # THE TWO STATES THIS BRANCH USED TO CONFLATE. "Admitted nothing" and "admitted
579	        # sources that carry no comparable identifier" are different facts and only the
580	        # first is vacuity; the old message asserted the second was the first, and told a
581	        # batch with two well-located sources that it was "missing its locators".
582	        if n_adm:
583	            fail("R9a", f"NOTHING IN SCOPE — {n_adm} source(s) admitted and not one carries a "
584	                        f"DOI or a URL, so no identifier exists to cross-check against the "
585	                        f"stash. That is not a locator problem to be waived: a source with no "
586	                        f"resolvable identifier at all cannot be cross-filed, deduplicated or "
587	                        f"re-retrieved by anyone. Give each admission its locator (R10).")
588	        elif n_search:
589	            # THE ZERO-YIELD BATCH, and it is a legitimate outcome rather than a hole.
590	            # The session ran searches and admitted nothing, which R14 calls a completed
591	            # unit of work. There is genuinely no identifier to cross-check, and saying so
592	            # is not the vacuity this rule guards against -- the guard is preserved by the
593	            # branch below, which still fires when NOTHING was logged either.
594	            ok("R9a", f"NOTHING TO CROSS-CHECK, and that is an honest result: {n_search} "
595	                      f"search(es) logged, 0 admissions. A zero-yield batch has no identifier "
596	                      f"to collide with the stash (R14: a zero-yield search is a completed "
597	                      f"unit of work)")
598	        else:
599	            fail("R9a", "NOTHING IN SCOPE — this batch admitted no sources AND logged no "
600	                        "searches, so nothing was examined and nothing was attempted. That is "
601	                        "an untouched or misnamed session, not a zero-yield one: check the "
602	                        "session id is the bare stem the DB stores (CLAUDE.md §7).")
603	    else:
604	        ok("R9a", f"{n_doi} admitted DOI(s) and {n_url} URL-only admission(s) checked against "
605	                  f"the stash; none held under a different ref_id")
606	
607	    # R9b WIDENED 2026-08-23. It compared DOIs only, so it reached 441 of 835 stash rows and
608	    # was blind to the other 394 -- yet CLAUDE.md 4's warning ("mint above the high-water mark
609	    # or you will collide with a held identifier") is not DOI-conditional. Comparing every
610	    # identifier the stash carries reaches 751 of 835. A row with NO identifier at all (84)
611	    # cannot be adjudicated either way and is deliberately out of reach, not silently included.
612	    ID_COLS = ("doi", "pmid", "pmcid", "isbn", "issn", "standard_number")
613	    conflict = " OR ".join(
614	        f"(COALESCE(e.{c},'') <> '' AND COALESCE(sl.{c},'') <> '' "
615	        f"AND LOWER(TRIM(sl.{c})) <> LOWER(TRIM(e.{c})))" for c in ID_COLS)
616	    collide = _rows(cx, f"SELECT e.ref_id, COALESCE(e.doi, e.pmid, e.isbn, e.issn, "
617	                        f"e.standard_number), COALESCE(sl.doi, sl.pmid, sl.isbn, sl.issn, "
618	                        f"sl.standard_number) FROM evidence_sources e "
619	                        f"JOIN source_locators sl ON sl.ref_id = e.ref_id "
620	                        f"WHERE ({conflict}){escope}", sargs)
621	    if collide:
622	        fail("R9b", f"{len(collide)} ref_id(s) admitted by this batch collide with a HELD "
623	                    f"identifier in source_locators that identifies a DIFFERENT source — mint "
624	                    f"above `db.py next-id ref`, which computes the high-water mark "
625	                    f"as the UNION of every table holding a ref_id -- NOT the stash alone: "
626	                    + "; ".join(f"{r} admitted {a}, stash holds {b}" for r, a, b in collide[:5]),
627	             len(collide))
628	    elif n_adm == 0 and n_search:
629	        ok("R9b", f"NOTHING TO COLLIDE, and that is an honest result: {n_search} search(es) "
630	                  f"logged, 0 admissions. A zero-yield batch mints no ref_id, so none can "
631	                  f"collide with a held identifier (R14)")
632	    elif n_adm == 0:
633	        fail("R9b", "NOTHING IN SCOPE — this batch admitted no sources AND logged no searches, "
634	                    "so the identifier collision check examined nothing and nothing was "
635	                    "attempted. An untouched or misnamed session, not a zero-yield one.")
636	    else:
637	        ok("R9b", f"{n_adm} admitted ref_id(s) checked against the stash across "
638	                  f"{len(ID_COLS)} identifier types; no collision")
639	
640	    # --- R10 locator re-retrieval ----------------------------------------------------------
641	    # HARDENED: the original accepted ANY non-empty locator field and never checked whether the
642	    # locator actually RESOLVED — 77 VERIFIED sources with unresolved DOIs passed silently.
643	    unver = _rows(cx, f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM evidence_sources WHERE verification_status='VERIFIED'"
644	                      f" AND COALESCE(doi,'')='' AND COALESCE(url,'')='' AND COALESCE(pmid,'')=''"
645	                      f" AND COALESCE(verified_by_tool,'')=''"
646	                      f"{scope}", sargs)[0][0]
647	    unresolved = _rows(cx, f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM evidence_sources WHERE "
648	                           f"verification_status='VERIFIED' AND COALESCE(doi,'') <> '' AND "
649	                           f"COALESCE(doi_resolution_outcome,'') NOT IN ('RESOLVED','NO-MATCH')"
650	                           f"{scope}", sargs)[0][0]
651	    if unver:
652	        fail("R10", f"{unver} VERIFIED source(s) with no locator or verifying tool. Ladder "
653	                    f"DOI -> Crossref/PubMed -> publisher -> repository; a publisher block is "
654	                    f"not a terminal answer.", unver)
655	    elif unresolved:
656	        fail("R10", f"{unresolved} VERIFIED source(s) carry a DOI whose resolution was never "
657	                    f"recorded (doi_resolution_outcome unset). Holding a DOI string is not "
658	                    f"re-retrieval — resolve it and record the outcome.")
659	    else:
660	        ok("R10", "every VERIFIED source has a locator AND a recorded resolution outcome")
661	
662	    # --- R10b unverified-status admission carrying a URL -----------------------------------
663	    # R10 above examines VERIFIED sources ONLY (its own comment, above). That is blind to the
664	    # condition that actually wakes the scheduled verify-urls cron: verify_urls.py:447-470
665	    # pools any source with `url<>'' AND verification_status IS NULL` and, for a non-empty
666	    # candidate set, writes a url_verification_runs row — a table NOT in
667	    # migration_reproducibility.EXEMPT_TABLES — then `.github/workflows/verify-urls.yml`
668	    # commits data/guidebook.db straight to main on its own schedule (cron: 0 06 1,15 * *).
669	    # `add-source` accepts a NULL --verification-status (db.py branches only on VERIFIED), so a
670	    # batch can admit exactly this row and pass every other rule. The next 1st/15th 06:00 UTC
671	    # fire then pushes a blob to main and reddens migration_reproducibility for every OPEN
672	    # DB-touching PR (2026-09-07 did this to PR #128; workplan/2026-09-10-road-to-batch-06.md
673	    # B3). Block the admission itself — the cron is owner decision #5 and is not this fix's to
674	    # edit (same workplan, STOP CONDITIONS #1).
675	    unverified_url = _rows(cx, f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM evidence_sources WHERE "
676	                               f"COALESCE(url,'') <> '' AND verification_status IS NULL"
677	                               f"{scope}", sargs)[0][0]
678	    # The subject: URL-bearing admissions. Without this the pass could not say whether it
679	    # had looked at anything, which is the whole of §5(a).
680	    n_url_bearing = _rows(cx, f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM evidence_sources WHERE "
681	                              f"COALESCE(url,'') <> ''"
682	                              f"{scope}", sargs)[0][0]
683	    if unverified_url:
684	        fail("R10b", f"{unverified_url} admitted source(s) carry a URL with verification_status "
685	                     f"left NULL. This is exactly the pool verify_urls.py's scheduled cron "
686	                     f"claims: the next 1st/15th 06:00 UTC fire will write a "
687	                     f"url_verification_runs row (not exempt from migration_reproducibility) "
688	                     f"and push a DB blob to main, reddening migration_reproducibility for "
689	                     f"every open DB-touching PR. Set --verification-status on add-source (even "
690	                     f"UNVERIFIED is a real value) before merge.", unverified_url)
691	    else:
692	        # SUBJECT COUNT, per this file's own DESIGN RULES and the R9a/R9b hardening
693	        # directly above: a bare PASS on a session that admitted nothing is CLAUDE.md
694	        # §5(a), and R10b shipped with exactly that on 2026-09-10.
695	        if not n_url_bearing:
696	            ok("R10b", "NOTHING IN SCOPE — this batch admitted no source carrying a URL, "
697	                       "so the cron's pool cannot have grown. EXAMINED: 0")
698	        else:
699	            ok("R10b", f"EXAMINED: {n_url_bearing} admitted source(s) carrying a URL; "
700	                       f"none left verification_status NULL")
701	
702	    # --- R11 vocabulary provenance ---------------------------------------------------------
703	    noprov_scope = _rows(cx, f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM term_aliases WHERE 1=1"
704	                       f"{scope}", sargs)[0][0]
705	    noprov = _rows(cx, f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM term_aliases WHERE COALESCE(notes,'')=''"
706	                       f"{scope}", sargs)[0][0]
707	    if noprov:
708	        fail("R11", f"{noprov} alias(es) with no sourcing note. No back-translation: every alias "
709	                    f"needs its authoritative in-language basis or [UNVERIFIED-TERMS].", noprov)
710	    else:
711	        # EXAMINED, per CLAUDE.md §2(a). This printed "all vocabulary carries
712	        # in-language sourcing provenance" over ZERO aliases for batch 05 -- and
713	        # corpus-wide 856 of 2382 aliases have no note, so the sentence was not merely
714	        # uninformative, it was the opposite of the corpus truth. A scoped count must
715	        # state its scope.
716	        ok("R11", f"{noprov_scope} alias(es) written by this batch; all carry "
717	                  f"in-language sourcing provenance" if noprov_scope else
718	                  "EXAMINED: 0 aliases. This batch wrote none, so this asserts "
719	                  "nothing about the corpus")
720	
721	    # R11's second half, added 2026-09-03: the D-0173 concept-vocabulary harvest.
722	    # The subject is THIS BATCH'S ADMISSIONS, not this session's writes — a later
723	    # session harvesting batch 05's nine sources satisfies the requirement, and
724	    # scoping on observed_terms.created_by_session would have called that a miss.
725	    # What this asserts is ONLY that every source the batch admitted carries at
726	    # least one observation. Whether the phrases harvested are the RIGHT ones is
727	    # not machine-decidable and is not claimed here; judgment adjudicates them
728	    # through term_adjudications, and the adversarial pass is where coverage is
729	    # argued. Do not "strengthen" this message: the weaker sentence is the true one.
730	    #
731	    # Why it exists at all, against §1's burden of proof: migration 068 shipped the
732	    # table, the writer AND a contract line ordering agents to harvest as they go,
733	    # and batch 05 admitted nine sources and harvested nothing. Nobody noticed until
734	    # someone counted the rows by hand a day later. Without this line the harvest is
735	    # a rule with no reader, which §1 calls the same defect as an unread field.
736	    unharvested = _rows(cx,
737	        "SELECT e.ref_id FROM evidence_sources e WHERE NOT EXISTS ("
738	        "SELECT 1 FROM observed_terms o WHERE o.ref_id = e.ref_id)" + escope, sargs)
739	    harvested = _rows(cx,
740	        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM observed_terms o WHERE EXISTS ("
741	        "SELECT 1 FROM evidence_sources e WHERE e.ref_id = o.ref_id" + escope + ")",
742	        sargs)[0][0]
743	    if unharvested:
744	        fail("R11-harvest",
745	             "%d admitted source(s) with no observed_terms row: %s. D-0173 harvests the "
746	             "concept vocabulary AT EVIDENCE, in the source's own words: "
747	             "db.py observe-term --ref-id ... --surface-form ..." % (
748	                 len(unharvested), ", ".join(r[0] for r in unharvested[:8])),
749	             len(unharvested))
750	    else:
751	        ok("R11-harvest",
752	           "%d concept observation(s) across this batch's admissions; every admitted "
753	           "source carries at least one. Whether they are the RIGHT phrases is NOT "
754	           "tested here — judgment adjudicates them" % harvested if harvested else
755	           "EXAMINED: 0 sources. This batch admitted none, so this asserts nothing")
756	
757	
758	    # --- R12 structured homes used ----------------------------------------------------------
759	    econ_words = _rows(cx, f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM search_executions WHERE ("
760	                           f"LOWER(COALESCE(findings_note,'')) LIKE '%cost%' OR "
761	                           f"LOWER(COALESCE(findings_note,'')) LIKE '%grant%' OR "
762	                           f"LOWER(COALESCE(findings_note,'')) LIKE '%bcr%'){scope}", sargs)[0][0]
763	    # HARDENED: threshold was "table is empty", so ONE row satisfied it permanently while any
764	    # amount of economic data stayed in prose. Now proportionate to the prose findings observed.
765	    econ_rows = _rows(cx, "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM economics_entries")[0][0]
766	    if econ_words and econ_rows < econ_words:
767	        fail("R12", f"{econ_words} search(es) carry economic findings in prose but only "
768	                    f"{econ_rows} economics_entries row(s) exist. Economic/case-study/value data "
769	                    f"belongs in economics_entries / case_studies / research_code_leads, not "
770	                    f"in prose notes.", econ_words)
771	    else:
772	        ok("R12", f"structured homes used (economics_entries={econ_rows} for {econ_words} "
773	                  f"prose findings)")
774	
775	    # --- R13 POPULATION-OF-STUDY vs POPULATION-SERVED ---------------------------------------
776	    # LESSON (2026-07-25): the highest-frequency silent error in this session was admitting a
777	    # source for a population it did not study. Twice caught only because linkage was done by
778	    # hand: Jinno 2007 is a CHAMBER EMISSIONS test with no human participants, filed against COM;
779	    # Amos 2019 is a GENERAL-POPULATION autistic-TRAITS sample, filed against AUT. Both are
780	    # legitimate as PROXY evidence and dangerous as anything else. An admission with no population
781	    # match asserts, silently, that study population == served population.
782	    anchors = _rows(cx, f"SELECT ref_id FROM evidence_sources WHERE tier BETWEEN 1 AND 3"
783	                        f"{scope}", sargs)
784	    unmatched = [r[0] for r in anchors
785	                 if not _rows(cx, "SELECT 1 FROM evidence_population_match WHERE ref_id=?",
786	                              (r[0],))]
787	    if unmatched:
788	        fail("R13", f"{len(unmatched)} tier-1..3 source(s) admitted with NO population match row "
789	                    f"— silently asserting that the population studied is the population served: "
790	                    f"{', '.join(unmatched[:5])}. Grade each EXACT/PARTIAL/PROXY and write the "
791	                    f"mismatch note.", len(unmatched))
792	    else:
793	        # Whether a mismatch_note is TRUE against the payload it describes is standing
794	        # subject 2 of the adversarial pass -- skills/adversarial-research_SKILL.md,
795	        # "Standing subjects of every adversarial pass". Named here so the gate points
796	        # at a home that exists; the phrase was in this file's R7 comment for a day
797	        # while no such section did.
798	        ok("R13", f"all {len(anchors)} tier-1..3 admissions carry a population match "
799	                  f"ROW -- presence only. Nothing here reads match_grade or "
800	                  f"mismatch_note, so 'graded' was an overclaim and is gone")
801	
802	    # --- R14 ZERO-YIELD MUST SAY WHY ---------------------------------------------------------
803	    # LESSON: a zero-yield search is only evidence of ABSENCE if the query was well-formed. Twice
804	    # this session an over-conjunctive PubMed query returned 0 and the honest reading was "wrong
805	    # query shape", not "no evidence exists" — PubMed AND-chains every term, so descriptive
806	    # multi-concept phrasings return nothing. Recording the empty without that distinction
807	    # silently converts a method failure into a finding of absence.
808	    bare_empty = _rows(cx, f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM search_executions WHERE results_found = 0 AND "
809	                           f"deferred_reason IS NULL AND COALESCE(findings_note,'') = ''{scope}",
810	                       sargs)[0][0]
811	    if bare_empty:
812	        fail("R14", f"{bare_empty} zero-yield search(es) carry no findings_note. Keep the empty "
813	                    f"(R8) but say WHICH it is: query-shape failure, wrong index, or genuine "
814	                    f"absence. Only the last is evidence.", bare_empty)
815	    else:
816	        ok("R14", "every zero-yield search records why it was empty")

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	scripts/generate/research_contract_hook.py — derive the SessionStart hook payload
4	from governance/research-contract.yaml.
5	
6	The R1-R15 contract used to exist as two hand-transcribed copies with no
7	comparator: the hook text in .claude/settings.json and the rule table in

2	description: Open a session correctly — set CURRENT before the first Bash call, or the command log lands in someone else's record
3	argument-hint: "[short-slug, defaults to the branch name]"
4	---
5	
6	Do this FIRST, before any other work. `scratchpad/CURRENT` moves at OPEN, and the
7	`PostToolUse` hook writes every Bash call to whatever it names. Leave it stale and
8	this session's commands append to a merged PR's record — measured twice in this
9	repository, most recently 2026-09-18.
10	
11	**`CURRENT` holds the DB SESSION STEM** (`session_YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>`), not a bare
12	branch slug. Batches 11–15 wrote branch slugs and their rows were stamped
13	`session_2026-09-18-research-batch-15-...` — a mismatch that scopes any check reading
14	`CURRENT` (e.g. `adversarial_pass_recorded`, RC4) to zero rows while reporting green.
15	
16	**THE FOLDER NAME AND `CURRENT`'S CONTENT MUST BE IDENTICAL, not just similar.**
17	`.claude/hooks/record-command.py` only honours `CURRENT` when
18	`scratchpad/<CURRENT's content>` is a real directory; otherwise it falls back to a
19	same-harness-sid guess that can misfile the whole command log into an unrelated past
20	session's folder (measured 2026-09-27, ~30 minutes of commands lost into a stale
21	directory after a session changed `CURRENT` to the stem without renaming its folder to
22	match). Create the folder AS the stem from the start — never a bare slug — so there is
23	no window where they disagree:
24	
25	```
26	SLUG="${1:-$(git branch --show-current | sed 's|.*/||')}"
27	STEM="session_$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)-${SLUG}"
28	mkdir -p "scratchpad/$STEM"
29	echo "$STEM" > scratchpad/CURRENT
30	cat scratchpad/CURRENT
31	```
32	
33	Rename the folder with `git mv` once the PR number exists, per the trap CLAUDE.md
34	section 7 names — but leave `scratchpad/CURRENT`'s content as the DB stem; do not
35	rename it to match. The hook's fallback (matching a `session_`/`pr-`-prefixed folder
36	by this harness's own last-logged command) covers exactly this gap, so a rename that
37	keeps one of those two prefixes stays routed correctly with no direct-match window at
38	all. What breaks routing is changing `CURRENT` to a value that names NEITHER the
39	current folder NOR any `session_`/`pr-`-prefixed folder that exists — always know
40	which of the two you are changing, and if it is `CURRENT`, create or rename the
41	matching folder in the same breath.
42	
43	**Record the session kind (RC6).** Say, in your first status update, whether this is a
44	**research session** (writes rows only — evidence, judgment, synthesis) or a **tooling
45	session** (schema, scripts, checks, governance prose — no research rows). This
46	determines whether `research_tooling_separation` should ever see both kinds of path in
47	one changeset from this session: it shouldn't, by construction, for either kind. A
48	session that finds it needs both mid-way is the RC6 trap (DR-2026-08-19 §12.2's AMENDED
49	callout): file the writer gap as a GAP and either leave the rows unwritten or write them
50	through verbs the CLI already has; the tooling fix ships in its own PR, merged to main
51	first, and the batch branch takes it with `git merge origin/main`.
52	
53	Then confirm the previous session closed cleanly:
54	
55	```
56	python3 scripts/preserve_transcripts.py --check
57	```
58	
59	`--check` is red for the whole life of a live session by construction — the
60	orchestrator's own transcript is still growing. Read it for what is unpreserved
61	from BEFORE this session, not as a gate on this one.
62

---
name: antagonist
description: >-
  Read-only adversarial critic. Use after any substantive piece of work — a
  research batch, a migration, a reasoning document, a diff — to attack the claim
  before it is ratified. Pairs with a separate writer that does the repair. Use
  when the request says adversarial, agonist-antagonist, critique, or "check this
  properly". Do NOT use it to write, fix, or plan the repair.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
model: fable
---

You attack the claim. You have no write access and you do not propose repairs —
proposing the fix is how a critic talks itself into accepting the thing.

**What you are looking for, in this order:**

1. **A gate that passed having examined nothing.** This repository's
   most-produced defect, four separate times. For every check cited as evidence,
   ask what its SUBJECT was. `EXAMINED: 0` under a PASS is not a pass. A session
   id in the wrong form (`.md` where the DB holds a bare stem) scopes a gate to
   zero rows and reports green.
2. **A number that could be wrong tomorrow with nothing going red.** Literals,
   thresholds, `min_items`, lists, globs, and sentences of prose restating a
   checked value. Prose callers are swept by no gate at all. Recompute every
   figure you are asked to accept.
3. **A claim the artifact does not support.** Read the artifact, not the summary
   of it. A 0-row object is unproven, not clean.
4. **A ruling that was already made.** Owner rulings supersede ratified records
   on contact and live overwhelmingly in `sessions/`, which `.ignore` hides from
   ripgrep and the Grep tool. Use `grep -r` or `git grep`. Never report a ruling
   absent from a search that could not have seen it.
5. **A fabricated or unverified bibliographic field.** On 2026-08-19 five sources
   were stored with invented co-authors — including the deletion of autistic
   community co-authors from a Co-1 paper whose entire warrant is their
   co-authorship — and six gates passed it, because each asked whether the
   fields were populated, never whether they were true. Diff stored data against
   the persisted payload in `retrieval-log/`.

**Read-only, always.** The database opens as
`sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro', uri=True)`. If asked to write,
refuse and say why.

**Report shape.** One finding per block: artifact and line, the claim, the failure
case that breaks it, and the command that shows it. Rank worst first. No false
balance — if eight things are broken, report eight. Say
`[NULL: <scope examined> — examined, nothing found]` where you found nothing;
silence reads as absence and absence is a finding you did not make.

Do not soften. Do not summarize the work back. Do not close with a verdict on
whether the work is "good overall".

**The eleven lenses.** Every one of these must appear at least once in your closing
block before the pass can be closed, whatever you numbered your prose findings above:

| Lens | What it tests |
|---|---|
| `L1-existence` | The source/row/artefact cited actually resolves — it exists. |
| `L2-fidelity` | The artefact says what the claim says it says. |
| `L3-independence` | Not the same dataset or evidence counted twice under two names. |
| `L4-tier` | Wrong tier or evidence-type, in either direction. |
| `L5-population` | Study population vs. served population, graded honestly. |
| `L6-contrary` | Was a "nothing found" a real absence or a search-shape failure? |
| `L7-recognition` | Would the population this serves recognise the claim as faithful? |
| `L8-query-shape` | A zero-yield search: query-shape failure vs. wrong index vs. genuine absence. |
| `S1-harm-reached-row` | A flagged harm/failure finding actually reached the row it should. |
| `S2-mismatch-note-vs-payload` | A recorded `mismatch_note` is true against the actual payload. |
| `S3-containment` | The fix stayed inside its stated blast radius — nothing else moved. |

**Closing block — required, so this pass can be recorded (RC4).** Put this fenced block
inside your FINAL report — the message you hand back when you finish (in this harness
that is your `SubagentHandback` call; a plain trailing text turn after it is not read).
One entry per finding, in this exact shape, so `db.py record-adversarial-pass` can read
it without anyone retyping a finding by hand:

```json adversarial-findings
[
  {"lens": "L2-fidelity", "subject_table": "search_candidates", "subject_key": "124",
   "claim_attacked": "candidate 124's exec_id names the search that surfaced it",
   "method": "compared the typed exec_id against the locator's own prose",
   "artefact": "retrieval-log/<session>/<file>.json", "verdict": "SUSTAINED",
   "severity": "HIGH"},
  {"lens": "L6-contrary", "subject_table": null, "subject_key": null,
   "claim_attacked": "no evidence of X was found",
   "method": "re-ran the search under a second query shape",
   "artefact": null, "verdict": "NOT-ATTACKED"}
]
```

`verdict` is `SUSTAINED` (the claim broke — set `severity` to one of `CRITICAL` / `HIGH`
/ `MEDIUM` / `LOW`, required for this verdict and refused for every other one), `SURVIVED`
(you attacked it and it held — name the `artefact` you attacked it WITH, per
DR-2026-09-11 clause 2, in more than a few characters, or the row is refused at close
time), `NOT-ATTACKED` (you did not reach this lens — say why in `method`, in a real
sentence, not a placeholder), or `WITHHELD-FOR-OWNER` (a doctrinal question, not a
factual one). At least one row must be SURVIVED — a zero-finding pass has to be able to
show what it attacked, or it is indistinguishable from a pass that never ran. This block
is what makes the pass exist as a checkable record rather than only as this transcript;
write it even when every lens comes back clean, and even when a lens is NOT-ATTACKED
because it plainly does not apply to this diff — say so in `method` rather than omitting
the row.

CREATE TABLE "base_parameters" (

    term_id             TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES terms(term_id),

    merged_into         INTEGER REFERENCES base_parameters(parameter_id),
    notes               TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT    NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT    NOT NULL,

    CHECK ((status = 'merged' AND merged_into IS NOT NULL)
        OR (status <> 'merged' AND merged_into IS NULL))

    canonical_en        TEXT NOT NULL,

CREATE TABLE term_adjudications (

    observation_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES observed_terms(observation_id),
    -- OUTCOMES, documented HERE and not inside the CHECK. dbcore.check_values() reads
    -- this constraint's own value list to build the CLI's refusal, and an inline
    -- comment between the quoted values defeats its parser -- measured 2026-09-03,
    -- when a first cut of this migration carried the descriptions inside the IN(...)

                            ('NAMES-EXISTING','NAMES-NEW','NOT-OURS','DEFERRED')),
    term_id             TEXT REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    -- NOT NULL: an adjudication that does not say why cannot be contested, and the
    -- whole point of splitting observation from judgment is that the judgement is
    -- inspectable.
    rationale           TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT,
    updated_by_session  TEXT,
    -- The outcome and the pointer must agree. An outcome that names a term must name
    -- one; an outcome that declines must not.
    CHECK (
        (outcome IN ('NAMES-EXISTING','NAMES-NEW') AND term_id IS NOT NULL)
     OR (outcome IN ('NOT-OURS','DEFERRED')        AND term_id IS NULL)

)

DDL observed_terms:
CREATE TABLE observed_terms (
    observation_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    -- POINTER, not a copy. The source's bibliography stays in evidence_sources.
    ref_id              TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
    -- The phrase EXACTLY as the source writes it. Not normalised, not translated,
    -- not mapped. R11 forbids back-translation and this is where that starts.
    surface_form        TEXT NOT NULL,
    -- The language the phrase APPEARS IN, which need not be the source's language.
    language            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'EN',
    -- R3's locator discipline: where in the source it appears.
    locator             TEXT,
    -- Enough surrounding text that judgment can adjudicate without re-retrieving.
    context_quote       TEXT,
    notes               TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT,
    updated_by_session  TEXT,
    -- One observation per phrase per language per source. A second sighting of the
    -- same phrase in the same source is the same fact.
    UNIQUE (ref_id, surface_form, language)
)

DDL source_value_extractions:
CREATE TABLE "source_value_extractions" (
  extraction_id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,

  -- THE HAND-OFF KEY (D-0168; pinned by the blocking judgment_handoff_shape check):
  -- NOT NULL, a real FK at the evidence item, and NO UNIQUE index over it anywhere.
  ref_id                 TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),

  -- The slug this extraction was MINED UNDER. Not a copy of source_slug_links: that
  -- junction says the source is admitted to the slug; this says the reading happened
  -- there. `evidence_sources` has no slug column, so there is nothing to point at.
  slug                   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES slugs(slug),

  -- THE SUBJECT (owner 2026-08-26), now mandatory. Was nullable with `parameter` /
  -- `parameter_canonical` beside it; a NOT NULL free-text parameter NAME sitting next to
  -- a mandatory pointer at the registry that holds that same name is the dual home rule 5
  -- forbids. The name is reached: base_parameters.term_id -> terms.canonical_en.
  --
  -- AND THE VERBATIM PHRASE IS NOT LOST WITH IT. `parameter` was documented (schemas/
  -- source_value_extraction.py) as "the SOURCE's own phrase for what it measures,
  -- verbatim and unjudged (R11/D-0173)". That fact already has a purpose-built home with
  -- a live writer and 33 live rows: `observed_terms.surface_form`, whose own DDL comment
  -- reads "The phrase EXACTLY as the source writes it. Not normalised, not translated,
  -- not mapped. R11 forbids back-translation and this is where that starts" -- keyed
  -- UNIQUE (ref_id, surface_form, language), with `locator` and `context_quote`, written
  -- by `db.py observe-term` and adjudicated by `adjudicate-term` (migration 068, D-0173).
  -- CLAUDE.md §6 orders exactly that split: "harvest concepts at evidence (db.py
  -- observe-term, verbatim and unjudged), adjudicate at judgment." `parameter` was the
  -- duplicate, and an UNREALISED one -- 0 rows, no writer, ever. Clause-level verbatim
  -- survives here in `claim_text` ("exact source phrasing") plus `source_section` and the
  -- 16 `loc_*` columns.
  --
  -- KNOWN RESIDUAL, stated rather than papered over: an extraction cannot say WHICH of
  -- its source's observations it was read from. Closing that is an `observation_id`
  -- pointer, and it is NOT added here because nothing would read it -- "an unread field,
  -- an uncalled script and an unregistered check are the same defect" (CLAUDE.md §8). Add
  -- it in the change that gives it a reader.
  parameter_id           INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES base_parameters(parameter_id),

  -- THE FOUR LENSES (owner 2026-08-28; CHECK relaxed by D-0182). Real typed FKs, one per
  -- lens, nothing polymorphic. They replace `population_code` (retired by that ruling's
  -- own ACTION) and `population_label`, the free-text companion that had no registry at
  -- all -- retiring the typed column while keeping the untyped one beside it would keep
  -- the exact defect the ruling was issued against.
  --
  -- `base_taxonomy_medical` holds 0 rows today, so a NON-NULL medical_code is
  -- unwritable until it is seeded. That is the CLAUDE.md §4 trap, and it is harmless in
  -- this shape precisely because the column is nullable and the CHECK is "at least one":
  -- the table stays writable through any of the other three. `specifications` carries the
  -- identical arrangement from 071.
  identity_code          TEXT REFERENCES populations(population_code),
  icf_code               TEXT REFERENCES base_icf(icf_code),
  needs_code             TEXT REFERENCES access_needs(need_code),
  medical_code           TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_medical(medical_code),

  jurisdiction           TEXT,
  setting                TEXT,

  claim_type             TEXT NOT NULL
                           CHECK (claim_type IN ('numerical','range','qualitative','framework','absent')),
  claimed_value          TEXT,
  claimed_unit           TEXT,
  claim_text             TEXT,
  source_section         TEXT,

  -- Value genealogy / independence substrate (DR-2026-07-13 H1), carried across
  -- unchanged. v_value_independence counts distinct roots over these.
  root_id                TEXT,
  root_type              TEXT
                           CHECK (root_type IN (
                             'measurement_primary', 'participatory_finding',
                             'committee_assertion', 'derived_calculation', 'untraced')),
  root_ref_id            TEXT REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
  echo_of                TEXT,
  measurement_paradigm   TEXT
                           CHECK (measurement_paradigm IN (
                             'swept_path_dynamic', 'static_turning_circle', 'static_clearance',
                             'anthropometric_percentile', 'instrumented_physical_measurement',
                             'route_metric', 'field_observation', 'participatory_spatial',
                             'stated_unmeasured')),
  device_class           TEXT
                           CHECK (device_class IN (
                             'manual_self_propelled', 'manual_attendant', 'power_chair', 'scooter',
                             'bariatric_manual', 'bariatric_power', 'walker_rollator',
                             'mixed', 'not_device_scoped')),
  root_population_note   TEXT,
  root_classification_basis TEXT,
  contested              INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
                           CHECK (contested IN (0, 1)),
  file_anchor            TEXT,

  -- Pinpoint locator hierarchy (migration 053), carried across unchanged. These are the
  -- clause-level address that makes D-0168's 1:N fan-out legible: NBC 3.8's many clauses
  -- are many rows, and these columns are what tells them apart.
  locator_scheme         TEXT,
  loc_division           TEXT,
  loc_part               TEXT,
  loc_section            TEXT,
  loc_subsection         TEXT,
  loc_paragraph          TEXT,
  loc_clause             TEXT,
  loc_subclause          TEXT,
  loc_division_end       TEXT,
  loc_part_end           TEXT,
  loc_section_end        TEXT,
  loc_subsection_end     TEXT,
  loc_paragraph_end      TEXT,
  loc_clause_end         TEXT,
  loc_subclause_end      TEXT,
  loc_note               TEXT,

  extraction_method      TEXT NOT NULL
                           CHECK (extraction_method IN ('skim','full-read','re-read','auto-mined')),
  extraction_status      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'preliminary'
                           CHECK (extraction_status IN ('preliminary','reviewed','verified','contradicted','absent-confirmed')),
  promoted_to_rdc_id     TEXT REFERENCES reasoning_doc_citations(citation_id),
  notes                  TEXT,

  created_at             TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_by_session     TEXT,
  updated_at             TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_by_session     TEXT, figure_role TEXT
  CHECK (figure_role IS NULL OR figure_role IN ('claim', 'finding', 'condition', 'derived')), comparator TEXT
  CHECK (comparator IS NULL OR comparator IN ('=', '<', '<=', '>', '>=', 'between', 'approx')),

  -- Carried across verbatim: if claim_type='absent', claimed_value must be NULL; if it
  -- is anything else, claimed_value must be present. `db.py add-extraction` refuses both
  -- violations in words BEFORE the INSERT, so an operator gets a sentence rather than
  -- "CHECK constraint failed".
  CHECK (
    (claim_type =  'absent' AND claimed_value IS NULL) OR
    (claim_type <> 'absent' AND claimed_value IS NOT NULL)
  ),

  -- D-0182, mechanised. Absence in a lens is fine; absence in ALL of them is not.
  -- Identical in form to specifications' and item_taxonomy_links' own CHECK.
  CHECK (COALESCE(identity_code, icf_code, needs_code, medical_code) IS NOT NULL)
)

9	renderer. This tool then extracts the delta as SQL, which feeds the ordinary
10	`emit_data_migration.py --input` and its ENUM/RANGE guards.
11	
12	    python3 scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py --scratch batch01.db --out batch01.sql
13

15	only canonical write in a research session remains `migrate_db.py`.
16	
17	The walk is additive by design. A row present in canonical but absent from the
18	scratch is REFUSED rather than rendered as a DELETE: a research batch adds
19	evidence, and a missing row means the scratch drifted from the canonical base
20	(usually a stale copy), which is a mistake to surface, not to replay.
21	
22	ONE NARROW EXCEPTION, opt-in (2026-09-26). Some db.py writers delete on purpose --
23	`unlink-admission` removes a wrong search_admissions edge -- and an additive-only
24	capture made that sanctioned write impossible to ship. `--allow-delete TABLE` renders
25	the missing rows of TABLE as DELETEs, and only when a writer in scripts/ actually
26	deletes from TABLE (dbcore.deletable_tables, derived from the writers the way the
27	capture set is). Every other missing row is still refused, so a stale copy is still
28	caught, and a deletion never happens unless the operator names the table.
29	"""

32	import os
33	import sqlite3

35	from datetime import datetime, timezone

45	DEFAULT_CANONICAL = os.environ.get("GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH", "data/guidebook.db")

47	# FK order: a parent is always emitted before anything that references it, so
48	# the migration applies cleanly even with foreign_keys enforcement on.
49	# TABLES MOVED TO scripts/dbcore.py 2026-08-25 and is imported below.
50	#
51	# WHY: this list and db.py's write coverage were two separate homes of one fact --
52	# "which tables a session may write" -- and that is exactly how a table became
53	# writable-but-invisible to capture. A rescue wrote 8 source_locators rows and this
54	# tool emitted 32 statements instead of 40, losing them with NO ERROR RAISED.
55	#
56	# THAT FIX WAS THE WRONG SHAPE, corrected 2026-09-13. One constant with two importers
57	# stopped the CLI and this tool disagreeing WITH EACH OTHER; it did nothing about the
58	# constant disagreeing with db.py's actual write surface, which is where all eight
59	# blindnesses lived — four of them already present when the comment claiming "a table
60	# can never again be known to one and not the other" was written. The set is now
61	# DERIVED from the writers by dbcore.writable_tables(conn), so a table is captured the
62	# moment something can write it. Ordering comes from the live FK graph, which also
63	# retired a real defect: the hand list placed evidence_population_match ahead of gaps,

67	def ro(path):
68	    return sqlite3.connect(f"file:{path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
69	
70	
71	def lit(v):
72	    """Render one value as a SQL literal."""
73	    if v is None:
74	        return "NULL"
75	    if isinstance(v, bool):
76	        return "1" if v else "0"
77	    if isinstance(v, int):
78	        return str(v)
79	    if isinstance(v, float):
80	        return repr(v)
81	    if isinstance(v, (bytes, bytearray)):
82	        return "X'" + v.hex() + "'"
83	    return "'" + str(v).replace("'", "''") + "'"
84	
85	
86	def columns(con, table):
87	    return [r[1] for r in con.execute('PRAGMA table_info("%s")' % table)]
88	
89	
90	def pk_columns(con, table):
91	    info = list(con.execute('PRAGMA table_info("%s")' % table))
92	    return [r[1] for r in sorted((r for r in info if r[5]), key=lambda r: r[5])]
93

95	def load(con, table, cols, pk):
96	    """Return {pk_tuple: {col: value}} for one table, ordered by primary key."""
97	    collist = ", ".join('"%s"' % c for c in cols)
98	    order = ", ".join('"%s"' % c for c in pk)
99	    rows = {}
100	    for r in con.execute('SELECT %s FROM "%s" ORDER BY %s' % (collist, table, order)):
101	        d = dict(zip(cols, r))
102	        rows[tuple(d[c] for c in pk)] = d
103	    return rows
104	
105	
106	def where(pk, row):
107	    return " AND ".join('"%s" = %s' % (c, lit(row[c])) for c in pk)

110	def emit(scratch_path, canonical_path, out_path, allow_delete=()):
111	    if scratch_path == canonical_path:
112	        sys.exit("ERROR: --scratch and --canonical are the same file. The scratch "
113	                 "must be a copy; the canonical DB is never written outside migrate_db.py.")
114	    sc, ca = ro(scratch_path), ro(canonical_path)
115	
116	    sv = sc.execute("PRAGMA user_version").fetchone()[0]
117	    cv = ca.execute("PRAGMA user_version").fetchone()[0]
118	    if sv != cv:
119	        sys.exit(f"ERROR: schema version mismatch — scratch is {sv}, canonical is {cv}. "
120	                 "Re-copy the scratch from the current canonical DB.")
121	
122	    # Derived per run from the live schema and the writers; never a module constant,
123	    # because a constant is what drifted eight times.
124	    tables = dbcore.writable_tables(ca)
125	    allow_delete = set(allow_delete or ())
126	    if allow_delete:
127	        not_deletable = sorted(allow_delete - dbcore.deletable_tables(ca))
128	        if not_deletable:
129	            sys.exit(f"ERROR: --allow-delete {not_deletable}: no sanctioned writer deletes from "
130	                     f"{'that table' if len(not_deletable) == 1 else 'those tables'} "
131	                     f"(dbcore.deletable_tables). A row missing there is drift, not a "
132	                     f"deletion to replay.")
133	    lines, n_ins, n_upd, missing = [], 0, 0, []
134	    deletes = {}
135	    for table in tables:
136	        cols = columns(ca, table)
137	        if not cols:
138	            sys.exit(f"ERROR: table {table} does not exist in the canonical DB.")
139	        if columns(sc, table) != cols:
140	            sys.exit(f"ERROR: column set for {table} differs between scratch and canonical. "
141	                     "Re-copy the scratch; do not hand-edit its schema.")
142	        pk = pk_columns(ca, table)
143	        if not pk:
144	            sys.exit(f"ERROR: {table} has no declared primary key; refusing to diff it "
145	                     "on implicit rowids, which are not stable across a rebuild.")
146	
147	        s_rows = load(sc, table, cols, pk)
148	        c_rows = load(ca, table, cols, pk)
149	        gone = [k for k in c_rows if k not in s_rows]
150	        if table in allow_delete:
151	            if gone:
152	                deletes[table] = ['DELETE FROM "%s" WHERE %s;' % (table, where(pk, c_rows[k]))
153	                                  for k in gone]
154	        else:
155	            missing += [(table, k) for k in gone]
156	
157	        inserts, updates = [], []
158	        for key, row in s_rows.items():                     # already PK-ordered
159	            if key not in c_rows:
160	                inserts.append('INSERT INTO "%s" (%s) VALUES (%s);' % (
161	                    table,
162	                    ", ".join('"%s"' % c for c in cols),
163	                    ", ".join(lit(row[c]) for c in cols)))
164	                continue
165	            changed = [c for c in cols if row[c] != c_rows[key][c]]
166	            if changed:
167	                updates.append('UPDATE "%s" SET %s WHERE %s;' % (
168	                    table,
169	                    ", ".join('"%s" = %s' % (c, lit(row[c])) for c in changed),
170	                    where(pk, row)))
171	        if inserts or updates:
172	            lines.append("-- %s: %d insert(s), %d update(s)" % (table, len(inserts), len(updates)))
173	            lines += inserts + updates
174	            lines.append("")
175	        n_ins += len(inserts)
176	        n_upd += len(updates)
177	
178	    if missing:
179	        for table, key in missing[:10]:
180	            print(f"  {table}: {key}", file=sys.stderr)
181	        sys.exit(f"ERROR: {len(missing)} row(s) exist in the canonical DB but not in the "
182	                 "scratch. The batch path is additive — this means the scratch was copied "
183	                 "from a different base, or rows were deleted. Refusing to emit. If a "
184	                 "sanctioned writer deleted them on purpose (unlink-admission), name the "
185	                 "table with --allow-delete.")
186	
187	    # Deletions first, children before parents (the reverse of the replay order), so a
188	    # DELETE never runs against a row a later statement in the same file still needs.
189	    n_del = 0
190	    del_lines = []
191	    for table in reversed(tables):
192	        if table in deletes:
193	            del_lines.append("-- %s: %d delete(s)" % (table, len(deletes[table])))
194	            del_lines += deletes[table] + [""]
195	            n_del += len(deletes[table])
196	    lines = del_lines + lines
197	
198	    if not lines:
199	        sys.exit("ERROR: no delta — the scratch is identical to the canonical DB across "
200	                 "all %d writable tables. Nothing to emit.\n"
201	                 "         If you believe you wrote rows, check they went to a table a "
202	                 "writer can reach: this compares exactly the tables scripts/db.py and "
203	                 "assess_cell.py INSERT into, minus %s." % (len(tables), sorted(dbcore.NOT_CAPTURED)))
204	
205	    header = [
206	        "-- Research batch delta, captured by scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py",
207	        "-- Captured:  %s" % datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
208	        "-- Scratch:   %s" % scratch_path,
209	        "-- Canonical: %s (schema version %d)" % (canonical_path, cv),
210	        "-- Totals:    %d insert(s), %d update(s), %d delete(s)" % (n_ins, n_upd, n_del),
211	        "--",
212	        "-- No transaction wrapper: the migration runner owns the boundary (F5).",
213	        "-- Feed this to: python3 scripts/emit_data_migration.py --input <this file>",
214	        "",
215	    ]
216	    text = "\n".join(header + lines).rstrip() + "\n"
217	    if out_path == "-":
218	        sys.stdout.write(text)
219	    else:
220	        with open(out_path, "w") as fh:
221	            fh.write(text)
222	        print("Wrote %s — %d insert(s), %d update(s), %d delete(s)"
223	              % (out_path, n_ins, n_upd, n_del))
224	    return 0

227	def selftest():
228	    """Prove the emitter round-trips, rather than asserting it."""
229	    import tempfile, os, shutil
230	    results, failures = [], 0
231	
232	    def check(name, cond, detail=""):
233	        nonlocal failures
234	        results.append((name, bool(cond), detail))
235	        if not cond:
236	            failures += 1
237	
238	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
239	        canon = os.path.join(tmp, "canon.db")
240	        con = sqlite3.connect(canon)
241	        con.execute('CREATE TABLE evidence_sources (ref_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT, year INT)')
242	        con.execute('CREATE TABLE source_slug_links (ref_id TEXT, slug TEXT, note TEXT, '
243	                    'PRIMARY KEY (ref_id, slug))')
244	        con.execute("INSERT INTO evidence_sources VALUES ('REF-1','existing',2020)")
245	        con.commit(); con.close()
246	
247	        scratch = os.path.join(tmp, "scratch.db")
248	        shutil.copy(canon, scratch)
249	        con = sqlite3.connect(scratch)
250	        con.execute("INSERT INTO evidence_sources VALUES ('REF-2','O''Brien; a title',2021)")
251	        con.execute("INSERT INTO source_slug_links VALUES ('REF-2','room-acoustic-performance',NULL)")
252	        con.execute("UPDATE evidence_sources SET year=2022 WHERE ref_id='REF-1'")
253	        con.commit(); con.close()
254	
255	        out = os.path.join(tmp, "batch.sql")
256	        # Narrow the walk to the fixture's two tables, and RESTORE it afterwards --
257	        # a module-global mutated by a test and left changed is a trap for any
258	        # caller that imports this module and runs selftest() before emit().
259	        _real_writable = dbcore.writable_tables
260	        dbcore.writable_tables = lambda _conn: ["evidence_sources", "source_slug_links"]
261	        emit(scratch, canon, out)
262	        sql = open(out).read()
263	        check("insert emitted", "INSERT INTO \"evidence_sources\"" in sql)
264	        check("update emitted, changed column only",
265	              'UPDATE "evidence_sources" SET "year" = 2022' in sql, sql)
266	        check("quote escaped", "'O''Brien; a title'" in sql)
267	        check("no transaction wrapper", "BEGIN" not in sql.upper().replace("BEGINNING", ""))
268	        check("parent table precedes child",
269	              sql.index("evidence_sources") < sql.index("source_slug_links"))
270	
271	        # applying the delta to a copy of canonical must reproduce the scratch
272	        replay = os.path.join(tmp, "replay.db")
273	        shutil.copy(canon, replay)
274	        con = sqlite3.connect(replay, isolation_level=None)
275	        # Strip comment LINES before splitting. Filtering whole chunks that start
276	        # with "--" would silently drop the statement following a comment header,
277	        # which is exactly the class of bug the runner's _code_of() exists to avoid.
278	        code = "\n".join(l for l in sql.splitlines() if not l.strip().startswith("--"))
279	        for stmt in [s for s in code.split(";\n") if s.strip()]:
280	            con.execute(stmt)
281	        got = con.execute("SELECT * FROM evidence_sources ORDER BY ref_id").fetchall()
282	        got_l = con.execute("SELECT * FROM source_slug_links").fetchall()
283	        con.close()
284	        con = sqlite3.connect(scratch)
285	        want = con.execute("SELECT * FROM evidence_sources ORDER BY ref_id").fetchall()
286	        want_l = con.execute("SELECT * FROM source_slug_links").fetchall()
287	        con.close()
288	        check("replay reproduces the scratch exactly", got == want and got_l == want_l,
289	              f"{got} vs {want}")
290	
291	        # determinism: two runs byte-identical apart from the timestamp header
292	        out2 = os.path.join(tmp, "batch2.sql")
293	        emit(scratch, canon, out2)
294	        strip = lambda t: "\n".join(l for l in t.splitlines() if not l.startswith("-- Captured:"))
295	        check("output is deterministic", strip(sql) == strip(open(out2).read()))
296	
297	        # a row missing from the scratch must be refused, not rendered as a DELETE
298	        con = sqlite3.connect(scratch)
299	        con.execute("DELETE FROM evidence_sources WHERE ref_id='REF-1'"); con.commit(); con.close()
300	        rc = 0
301	        try:
302	            emit(scratch, canon, os.path.join(tmp, "x.sql"))
303	        except SystemExit as e:
304	            rc = 1
305	            check("deletion refused with a reason", "additive" in str(e), str(e))
306	        check("deletion refused", rc == 1)
307	
308	        # ...unless the operator names the table AND a writer deletes from it
309	        _real_deletable = dbcore.deletable_tables
310	        dbcore.deletable_tables = lambda _conn: {"evidence_sources"}
311	        out3 = os.path.join(tmp, "batch3.sql")
312	        emit(scratch, canon, out3, allow_delete=["evidence_sources"])
313	        sql3 = open(out3).read()
314	        check("an allowed deletion is rendered as a keyed DELETE",
315	              """DELETE FROM "evidence_sources" WHERE "ref_id" = 'REF-1';""" in sql3, sql3)
316	        check("deletions precede inserts",
317	              sql3.index("DELETE FROM") < sql3.index("INSERT INTO"))
318	        replay3 = os.path.join(tmp, "replay3.db")
319	        shutil.copy(canon, replay3)
320	        con = sqlite3.connect(replay3, isolation_level=None)
321	        code3 = "\n".join(l for l in sql3.splitlines() if not l.strip().startswith("--"))
322	        for stmt in [s for s in code3.split(";\n") if s.strip()]:
323	            con.execute(stmt)
324	        got3 = con.execute("SELECT * FROM evidence_sources ORDER BY ref_id").fetchall()
325	        con.close()
326	        con = sqlite3.connect(scratch)
327	        want3 = con.execute("SELECT * FROM evidence_sources ORDER BY ref_id").fetchall()
328	        con.close()
329	        check("replay with the deletion reproduces the scratch exactly", got3 == want3,
330	              f"{got3} vs {want3}")
331	        dbcore.deletable_tables = lambda _conn: set()
332	        rc = 0
333	        try:
334	            emit(scratch, canon, os.path.join(tmp, "y.sql"), allow_delete=["evidence_sources"])
335	        except SystemExit as e:
336	            rc = 1
337	            check("--allow-delete on a table no writer deletes from is refused",
338	                  "no sanctioned writer" in str(e), str(e))
339	        check("--allow-delete without a deleting writer refused", rc == 1)
340	        dbcore.deletable_tables = _real_deletable

342	    dbcore.writable_tables = _real_writable
343	    print("\n--- emit_batch_sql selftest ---")
344	    for name, ok, detail in results:
345	        print("  %s: %s%s" % ("PASS" if ok else "**FAIL**", name,
346	                              ("  [%s]" % detail) if not ok else ""))
347	    print("\nRESULTS: %d/%d selftest cases pass" % (len(results) - failures, len(results)))
348	    print("SELFTEST: %s" % ("FAIL" if failures else "PASS"))
349	    return 1 if failures else 0

352	def main():
353	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
354	    p.add_argument("--scratch", help="Session scratch DB written by db.py under GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH")
355	    p.add_argument("--canonical", default=DEFAULT_CANONICAL,
356	                   help="Canonical DB to diff against (default: $GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH "
357	                        "or data/guidebook.db)")
358	    p.add_argument("--out", default="-", help="Write SQL here ('-' for stdout)")
359	    p.add_argument("--allow-delete", action="append", default=[], metavar="TABLE",
360	                   help="Render rows missing from the scratch in TABLE as DELETEs. Only for a "
361	                        "table a sanctioned writer deletes from (e.g. search_admissions, "
362	                        "unlink-admission); repeatable. Everything else stays additive.")
363	    p.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true", help="Run the round-trip tests and exit")
364	    args = p.parse_args()
365	    if args.selftest:
366	        sys.exit(selftest())
367	    if not args.scratch:
368	        p.error("--scratch is required (or use --selftest)")
369	    sys.exit(emit(args.scratch, args.canonical, args.out, allow_delete=args.allow_delete))
370	
371	
372	if __name__ == "__main__":
373	    main()

2	"""scripts/audit/adversarial_pass_audit.py — the pass exists for what this session wrote.
3	
4	WHY THIS EXISTS. Three canonical statements already require an adversarial pass on every
5	research/synthesis diff (the 2026-08-19 RULE; DR-2026-09-11 clause 2; pipeline-contract.yaml's
6	cross_stage/definition-of-done), and none of the three had a committed enforcer.
7	`claims_docket.py` scans for claim-words in prose; the word "adversarial" appears in its
8	comments only. Batch 20's own antagonist pass ran the SAME model as its author while its
9	record called it independent, and nothing caught that because nothing recorded a pass in
10	checkable form (DR-2026-09-26-recurring-defect-shapes-remediation.md, RC4).
11	
12	THE SUBJECT TABLES are not a list in this file (CLAUDE.md rule 8). They are parsed from the
13	2026-08-19 RULE's own text in references/project-standards.md, anchored on a quote that must
14	occur exactly once. If the ruling's wording ever moves, this audit exits 2 ("cannot run")
15	rather than silently examining nothing.
16	
17	THE COLUMNS are every column of those tables whose name ENDS in `_by_session` (a substring
18	match would wrongly catch bpc_metadata.supersession_check_complete). `connection_targets` is
19	NOT one of the RULE's limb-(a) tables and this script never touches it; it is named here only
20	because it is DR-2026-09-26 section 1.2's own example of why OQ-8's wider scope (every
21	writable table, not just the RULE's list) needs a separate design -- that table has no
22	`_by_session` column at all, so a widened version of this script would have to decide what
23	"this session wrote to it" even means there. This script's own subject, derived below, never
24	includes it.
25	
26	SCOPE IS THE RULE'S LIST, DELIBERATELY, until the owner answers OQ-8 (widen to every writable
27	table). Widening this file ahead of that answer would implement OQ-8 while the DR text says
28	it is still open.
29	
30	`CURRENT`, not `LATEST-RESEARCH`: the latter names the PREVIOUS session for the whole life of
31	the current one (CLAUDE.md section 7), so a mid-session check against it silently audits
32	someone else's batch. Accepts either spelling (bare stem or `<stem>.md`) when matching rows,
33	because CURRENT holds the bare form today but has not always (batches 11-15 wrote branch
34	slugs) and no row in any writable table carries the `.md` form (verified 2026-09-26).
35	"""
36	import json
37	import re
38	import sqlite3
39	import sys
40	from pathlib import Path
41	
42	sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
43	import dbcore                                                        # noqa: E402
44	
45	REPO_ROOT = dbcore.REPO_ROOT
46	DB_PATH = dbcore.db_path()
47	LEDGER = REPO_ROOT / "references" / "project-standards.md"
48	
49	_ANCHOR = ("An adversarial pass may be commissioned ONLY against a diff that (a) wrote "
50	           "rows to the research tables (")
51	
52	
53	def _rule_tables() -> list:
54	    """Table names parsed from the 2026-08-19 RULE's own limb (a), never listed here."""
55	    if not LEDGER.exists():
56	        return []
57	    text = LEDGER.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
58	    if text.count(_ANCHOR) != 1:
59	        return None
60	    i = text.index(_ANCHOR) + len(_ANCHOR)
61	    close = text.index(")", i)
62	    return re.findall(r"`([a-z_]+)`", text[i:close])
63	
64	
65	def main() -> int:
66	    if len(sys.argv) < 3 or sys.argv[1] != "--session":
67	        print("usage: adversarial_pass_audit.py --session <session-stem-or-.md>")
68	        print("EXAMINED: 0")
69	        return 2
70	    session = sys.argv[2]
71	    stem = session[:-3] if session.endswith(".md") else session
72	
73	    tables = _rule_tables()
74	    if tables is None:
75	        print(f"[ERROR] the RULE anchor occurs != 1 time in "
76	              f"{LEDGER.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)} -- the ruling's wording moved. Refusing "
77	              f"to guess the subject tables.")
78	        print("EXAMINED: 0")
79	        return 2
80	    if not tables:
81	        print(f"[ERROR] no subject tables parsed from {LEDGER.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}.")
82	        print("EXAMINED: 0")
83	        return 2
84	
85	    if not DB_PATH.exists():
86	        print(f"[ERROR] no database at {DB_PATH}.")
87	        print("EXAMINED: 0")
88	        return 2
89	    conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{DB_PATH}?mode=ro", uri=True)
90	    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
91	
92	    live = {t for (t,) in conn.execute(
93	        "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'")}
94	
95	    examined = 0
96	    per_table = {}
97	    for t in tables:
98	        if t not in live:
99	            continue
100	        cols = [c[1] for c in conn.execute(f'PRAGMA table_info("{t}")')
101	                if c[1].endswith("_by_session")]
102	        if not cols:
103	            continue  # a RULE table with no _by_session column has nothing this audit can match
104	        # ONE count per table, over an OR across every _by_session column it has — not
105	        # one count PER COLUMN summed. A table with both created_by_session and
106	        # updated_by_session double-counts a single row that matches on both under the
107	        # summed form; EXAMINED must be a row count, not a column-match count.
108	        where = " OR ".join(f'"{c}" IN (?, ?)' for c in cols)
109	        params = [v for _ in cols for v in (stem, stem + ".md")]
110	        n = conn.execute(f'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "{t}" WHERE {where}', params).fetchone()[0]
111	        if n:
112	            per_table[t] = n
113	        examined += n
114	
115	    print(f"Subject tables (RULE limb (a), derived): {sorted(tables)}")
116	    print(f"Session: {stem}")
117	    if per_table:
118	        print("Rows written into subject tables by this session:")
119	        for t, n in sorted(per_table.items()):
120	            print(f"  {t}: {n}")
121	    print(f"EXAMINED: {examined}")
122	
123	    if examined == 0:
124	        print("VERDICT: PASS — NOTHING-IN-SCOPE (this session wrote no rows into the "
125	              "RULE's subject tables; it owes no pass).")
126	        return 0
127	
128	    passes = conn.execute(
129	        "SELECT pass_id, closed_at, reviewer_models, author_models FROM adversarial_passes "
130	        "WHERE subject_session IN (?, ?)", (stem, stem + ".md")).fetchall()
131	    closed = [p for p in passes if p["closed_at"]]
132	
133	    if not closed:
134	        if passes:
135	            print(f"FAIL: {len(passes)} pass(es) recorded for this session, but none is "
136	                  f"CLOSED (close-adversarial-pass). An open pass is not a finished one.")
137	        else:
138	            print("FAIL: no adversarial_passes row names this session, and it wrote to "
139	                  "the RULE's subject tables. Record the pass (db.py "
140	                  "record-adversarial-pass), then close it.")
141	        return 1
142	
143	    reports = []
144	    for p in closed:
145	        try:
146	            rev = set(json.loads(p["reviewer_models"]))
147	            auth = set(json.loads(p["author_models"]))
148	        except (TypeError, ValueError):
149	            rev = auth = set()
150	        if rev & auth:
151	            reports.append(f"  pass {p['pass_id']}: reviewer/author model overlap {rev & auth} "
152	                           f"-- same-model pass. Whether this counts as independent is OQ-1, "
153	                           f"the owner's to answer; this audit only reports it.")
154	    undisposed = conn.execute(
155	        "SELECT f.finding_id FROM adversarial_findings f "
156	        "JOIN adversarial_passes p ON p.pass_id = f.pass_id "
157	        "WHERE p.subject_session IN (?, ?) AND f.verdict = 'SUSTAINED' "
158	        "AND f.disposition IS NULL", (stem, stem + ".md")).fetchall()
159	    if undisposed:
160	        reports.append(f"  {len(undisposed)} SUSTAINED finding(s) with no disposition: "
161	                       f"{[r['finding_id'] for r in undisposed]}")
162	
163	    if reports:
164	        print("REPORTED (not blocking):")
165	        print("\n".join(reports))
166	    print(f"VERDICT: PASS — {len(closed)} closed pass(es) recorded for this session.")
167	    return 0
168	
169	
170	if __name__ == "__main__":
171	    sys.exit(main())
